2026-08-12T03:50:40.7443621Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7444003Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7444350Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7444832Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7445216Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7445717Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7447274Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7449563Z >
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7451846Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7454227Z >
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7502613Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7503567Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7503798Z ### How to Use
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7504034Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7505014Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7505862Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7506031Z ```bash
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7506728Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7507480Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7508448Z ```
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7508660Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7508926Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7509452Z ```bash
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7510082Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7510902Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7511752Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7512476Z ```
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7512672Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7513311Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7514170Z ```bash
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7514729Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7515405Z ```
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7515603Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7516102Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7516691Z ```bash
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7517214Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7518312Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7519051Z ```
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7519258Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7519521Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7519943Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7521351Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7522913Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7523080Z ```bash
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7523507Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7524356Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7525168Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7525473Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7525931Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7526957Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7527784Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7528436Z ```
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7528636Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7529412Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7530315Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7530483Z ```bash
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7531150Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7532028Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7532724Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7533166Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7533570Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7534344Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7534872Z ```
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7535070Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7535265Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7536095Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7537056Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7538194Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7539206Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7540285Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7540809Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7540981Z ### Notes
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7541192Z 
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7541800Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7543219Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7569102Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7571756Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7575361Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7585710Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7588541Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7590570Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7592275Z <github-context>
2026-08-12T03:50:40.7597435Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:
